After several consecutive weeks where ChatGPT users were only subject to weekly usage limits, OpenAI announced today the restoration of the five-hour usage cap for Plus subscribers on Codex and ChatGPT Work. Details below.

ChatGPT Plus subscribers see return of five-hour usage cap

Thibault "Sibo" Sottiaux, head of engineering for OpenAI's Codex and ChatGPT, announced tonight that starting tomorrow (the 25th), Plus subscribers will regain the five-hour usage cap on Codex and ChatGPT Work.

Once users hit either the five-hour or weekly limit, they can either wait for the next cycle to reset, or purchase additional credits. OpenAI also occasionally resets users' usage limits for free, and stored reset counts can be earned through specific promotional campaigns and referral offers.

However, over the past few weeks, OpenAI had temporarily removed the five-hour cap on Codex and ChatGPT Work, keeping only the weekly limit in place.

During this period, the company had also repeatedly reset users' weekly limits early to celebrate milestones, including reaching an additional one million active users across the two (now merged) platforms.

Nonetheless, Sibo explained on X tonight:

"We will restore the five-hour usage cap for Plus accounts on ChatGPT Work and Codex tomorrow. I mentioned this before, but then postponed it. This is necessary because (a) the five-hour cap lets us smooth out the load on our compute resources, which keeps the weekly allowance generous, and (b) most Plus users are lighter and newer users who sometimes accidentally burn through their entire weekly allowance and then feel confused, resulting in a poor experience. Over the coming months, we will continue to not enforce the five-hour cap for the $100 and $200 Pro subscriptions."

Sibo made no mention of any changes for Enterprise or Edu accounts, which currently use a separate credit-based system.

Does the return of the five-hour cap on ChatGPT Work and Codex affect you? Let us know in the comments.
